doubts: RL classes on Macs as a market

first_impression: A Metal-fused env on a Mac with MuJoCo checks and a foot-slip story. Planar 2D is a toy, but I like it.
confusing: Slide 10 compares to MuJoCo's Python mj_step loop on a planar model, which is not MJX, Warp or Isaac
Slide 14 policy transfer is MuJoCo with a mirror model whose contacts differ, not a different simulator
Slide 9 shows the walker diverging from MuJoCo after 0.6-0.8 s, so the contact model is not validated for locomotion
doubts: 60x is mostly against a naive CPU loop. Same-algorithm GPU gain is only about 3.7x
Walker speed of 2.74 m/s might still exploit the contact model
The 19.8 vs 21.9 m transfer is only 90 percent, and the gap may hide the contact difference
questions: How does this compare to MJX or Warp on a 4090 in steps per second?
Is the policy robust to friction or mass randomization?
How many substeps and solver iterations, and is the solver stable at large timesteps?

fixes.change: Show the 3.7x GPU-only and 33x fusion split next to the headline, and add a multithreaded C MuJoCo number or a MJX reference if you have one
Add domain-randomized transfer (friction and mass +/-20 percent) to show robustness rather than one nominal match
Show the walker divergence time and cause on the slide, for example impulse vs soft contact, plus one metric for how final gait speed differs

doubts: Students do RL on Colab for free, and Apple may ship its own MLX robotics tooling
The market of RL classes with Macs and a need for 2D physics is tiny
Open source with no moat or pricing evidence
questions: Who pays, and how much per seat?
What stops Apple or Google from shipping this?
What is the path from 2D to the 3D that research and industry want?
How many students or teachers have you talked to?

first_impression: Fused Metal kernels, 4096 envs, CoreML export, and honest limits. This is the first Mac RL tool I would try.
confusing: Slide 5 annotation text runs off the right edge ('torque' cut) and the clamp line is truncated
Slide 6 3.2 days in 28 s, and slide 15 7.8 days in 1:06, mix steps x dt with wall time, so the experience figure is easy to question
Slide 14 MacGym 21.9 M label overlaps the dot bar
doubts: Planar 2D with ground-only contact and no self-collision limits what the policy proves
The 5-seed 54.9 m result and the 8 s evaluation numbers on slide 7 use different metrics
60x against Python mj_step is not a like-for-like speed test
questions: Can I plug in my own MJCF or URDF, and what does the compiler support?
Do PPO hyperparameters or reward shaping cause the walker to exploit the contact model?
